description: The firm's scheduled automations: op schedule puts an approved script on a timer, unschedule stops one, list joins scripts with their schedules, get reads one in full with its review history.

op.description: schedule: create a timer for an approved script. unschedule: stop one. list: every script with its schedules. get: one schedule in full.

script.description: The script file, e.g. 'dunning.py'. Required for schedule; on unschedule an alternative to name (pair with subject); on list a filter for one script's schedules.

schedule_expression.description: schedule only, required there: 'rate(3 days)', 'cron(0 9 * * ? *)', or 'at(2026-09-01T09:00:00)' for a single run.

subject.description: What a run is about — an invoice id, a contact. Distinguishes one schedule of a script from another (schedule), and finds it again (unschedule with script).

name.description: The schedule name as list reports it, e.g. 'auto-dunning-INV_1042'. Required for get; on unschedule an alternative to script+subject.

params.description: schedule only: arguments for the script's run(ctx, **params). Pass references (an incident id, a rule key), not copied values; they are read fresh each time it fires.

timezone.description: schedule only: IANA name, e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'. Defaults to UTC.

one_shot.description: schedule only: true for a schedule that deletes itself after it fires once. Use with an at() expression.

start_date.description: schedule only, ISO-8601 UTC: nothing runs before this.

end_date.description: schedule only, ISO-8601 UTC: the last moment it may run, after which it deletes itself. A repeat with no end_date runs until someone unschedules it.

rules.description: schedule only: `{subject: [instance rows]}` the script will ask for with ctx.rules. Resolved now and frozen — automate holds no table, so it cannot look them up when the schedule runs.
